label: copy-phase input token u (from the 3rd output on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is u (the model just emitted u, recall_idx >= 2, so the u is a re-input of original token at position >= 1). Never fires on u during the original phase or at the first copy output, and never fires on any other input token. 100% of activations have in_tok == u; about 85% of qualifying copy-phase u inputs activate. Magnitude grows with position in the copy phase: activity rate is lower at recall_idx 2 (~1.9%) than at recall_idx >= 3 (~3.2%), and the top activations (around 0.9-1.0 of max) occur late in long sequences (L = 8-9). A repeated u in the copy phase tends to activate more strongly on the later occurrence.

issues: The factual claims check out on the dev profile. Activity is 100% copy phase and 100% in_tok == u. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase. Recall_idx 0 has 0 activations and recall_idx 1 has 1. The rate is 1.9% at recall_idx 2 and about 3.1-3.3% at recall_idx >= 3. Test scores reproduce: P 0.853, R 1.0, F1 0.921, mass recall 1.0. Misses with --split test show 0 missed activations.

There is one systematic false-positive class, and the explanation already partly discloses it. About 67% of test false positives (7329 of 10927) fall at recall_idx == 2, where the fed-back u is orig(1). Precision there is 0.56, against 0.94 at recall_idx >= 3. Precision at recall_idx 2 also falls with length: 0.75 at L <= 4, 0.72 at L = 5, 0.55 at L = 6, 0.44 at L >= 7. It falls further when u repeats (in_count >= 2, precision 0.34). This looks like a graded positional ramp, not a separate concept. Patching it gives little on test: excluding (recall_idx == 2 & in_count >= 2) reaches F1 0.926; (recall_idx >= 3) | (recall_idx == 2 & L <= 5 & in_count == 1) reaches 0.919.

The false positives at recall_idx >= 3 are about 6% of predicted steps. No split I tried shows a clear pattern: correct, in_first, in_count, to_go, digit or vowel previous token, digit output token. They look like scattered noise.

Small wording problem in the label. At recall_idx == 2 the fed-back input is the model's 2nd output (orig(1)), not its 3rd. 'From the 3rd output on' is off by one about which output is the input; the predicate is right.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input token u (fed-back u from the model's 2nd output on; weaker and less reliable at the 2nd, especially in long sequences)
